items.q: Match the following pre-diabetes interventions — 1) Lifestyle 2) Metformin 3) Bariatric surgery 4) Insulin sensitisers (TZDs) … A) 7% weight loss + 150 min/week activity B) Considered in high-risk patients <60 yr C) For BMI ≥35 with comorbidities D) Pioglitazone reduced progression
items.exp: Lifestyle with 7% weight loss and 150 min/week activity is first-line; metformin is added in high-risk patients under 60; bariatric surgery is for BMI ≥35 with comorbidities; pioglitazone has RCT evidence for progression reduction. (Book p920)

items.q: A 45-year-old BMI 32 has pre-diabetes with HbA1c 6.3%. Three months of lifestyle change produced no improvement. The most consistent next step is:
items.exp: Metformin is added for high-risk pre-diabetes patients with persistent hyperglycaemia despite lifestyle change. (Book p920)

items.q: Assess pre-diabetes screening: I BMI ≥25 (printed as 'overweight') plus another risk factor is the threshold. II Screening begins at age 25–60 (printed '2–60').
items.exp: Screening is recommended for BMI ≥25 plus risk factors; ADA typically recommends starting at age 35, not 25–60 (note: the source's 'Age 2-60yrs' is an inconsistency that should be flagged as the typical ADA recommendation is ≥35). (Book p920)

items.q: Which is the odd one out among metformin contraindications?
items.exp: eGFR ≥45 is not a contraindication; the others are contraindications or cautions (eGFR <30 contraindication, hepatic failure and alcoholism caution). (Book p920)

items.q: The page's metformin dose threshold for withholding in CKD is eGFR < ___ mL/min/1.73 m².
items.exp: Metformin is contraindicated at eGFR <30; dose-reduced between 30–45. (Book p920)

items.q: Match the following target to the population — 1) Most non-pregnant adults with diabetes 2) Older / frail with comorbidities 3) Pregnancy with pre-existing diabetes … A) HbA1c <7% B) HbA1c 7.5–8% or higher C) HbA1c <6–6.5% if achievable without hypoglycaemia
items.exp: Most adults target HbA1c <7%; older frail patients tolerate 7.5–8%; pregnancy pre-existing diabetes aims for <6.5% if achievable safely. (Book p920)

items.q: An 80-year-old nursing-home resident with multimorbidities has T2DM and frequent hypoglycaemia. The most appropriate HbA1c target is:
items.exp: Elderly frail patients tolerate a relaxed target of 7.5–8% to avoid hypoglycaemia. (Book p920)

items.q: Assess targets: I A1c-Derived Average Glucose (ADAG) provides an estimated mean glucose. II SMBG is not needed with HbA1c.
items.exp: ADAG links HbA1c to mean glucose; SMBG remains essential, especially in insulin-treated patients. (Book p920)

items.q: Match the following SMBG pattern to population — 1) Type 1 on basal-bolus 2) Type 2 on metformin only 3) Pregnancy with GDM on insulin 4) Stable Type 2 with HbA1c 6.8% … A) ≥4 checks/day B) Less frequent, fasting or paired C) Frequent daily checks D) Routine not required
items.exp: Type 1 basal-bolus needs ≥4 checks/day; metformin-only T2DM benefits from fewer paired checks; GDM on insulin needs frequent checks; well-controlled T2DM may not need routine SMBG. (Book p920)

items.q: A T1DM patient on basal-bolus has HbA1c 8.5% with frequent hypoglycaemia. The next step is:
opts: Review SMBG data, adjust insulin and consider CGM
Stop SMBG and rely on HbA1c
items.exp: Frequent hypoglycaemia with elevated HbA1c prompts review of SMBG data, insulin adjustment and CGM to reduce variability. (Book p920)

items.q: Pre-diabetes is sometimes treated with ___ in high-risk women with prior gestational diabetes.
items.exp: Metformin is recommended in high-risk patients, including women with prior GDM. (Book p920)

items.q: Assess pre-diabetes: I A1c 6.0% is normal. II HbA1c ≥6% with risk factors is an indication for intervention.
items.exp: HbA1c 5.7–6.4% is pre-diabetes; ≥6% with risk factors is sufficient for intervention in many algorithms. (Book p920)
